title: Title & Registration Services Allocation of a Stated Fee Shortage Between Buyer and Kestrel
content:
For a Title & Registration Services order sent back by the state for a fee shortage, the buyer's cure share is the fraction of the stated shortage that the buyer pays: the cure payment is the stated shortage multiplied by the buyer's cure share. The cure share follows who made the packet wait before it went to the state.

## Late days on each side

- **The buyer's cure late days** are the calendar days from the buyer's cure document clock start to the date the order's latest document was received, less the service type's customer document due days, and never below zero.
- **Kestrel's cure late days** are the calendar days from Kestrel's cure handling clock start to the date of the order's most recent remittance to the state, less a handling allowance of five (5) calendar days, and never below zero.

## Decision table

| Buyer's cure late days | Kestrel's cure late days | Buyer's cure share |
|---|---|---|
| more than zero | more than zero | the buyer's cure late days divided by the sum of the buyer's and Kestrel's cure late days |
| zero | more than zero | zero |
| more than zero | zero | one: the buyer bears the whole stated shortage |
| zero | zero | one: the buyer bears the whole stated shortage |

Stated as a rule: when both the buyer and Kestrel have cure late days, the cure share is the buyer's cure late days divided by the sum of both sides' cure late days; when Kestrel has cure late days and the buyer has none, the cure share is zero; otherwise the cure share is one.

## Handling allowance at its boundary (hypothetical)

| Calendar days from Kestrel's clock start to the most recent remittance | Kestrel's cure late days |
|---|---|
| 4 | 0 |
| 5 | 0 |
| 6 | 1 |

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Service type with a 10-day document due period. The buyer's clock starts 1 March and the latest document arrives 25 March: 24 calendar days, less 10, gives 14 buyer late days. Kestrel's clock starts 25 March and the most recent remittance is dated 10 April: 16 days, less 5, gives 11 Kestrel late days. Both sides have late days, so the cure share is 14 divided by 25, that is 0.56. On a stated shortage of 50.00 the cure payment is 50.00 multiplied by 0.56, that is 28.00.
